home.faqTitle: What people ask before their first booking

notHome.q: What if I'm not home when the professional arrives?
notHome.a: You'll get a call and an SMS when they set off, so you know roughly when to expect them. If your plans change, cancel from the booking screen any time before they leave — there's no charge. If nobody is home when they arrive and we weren't told, your first time costs you nothing; after that the wasted trip is added to your next booking, because somebody rode across town for it.

price.a: Every category has a published rate for common jobs, and you see the estimate before you confirm. If the professional finds the job is bigger than described — a burst pipe rather than a dripping tap — they'll explain why and you approve the revised price before they carry on. Nothing gets added to your bill without your say-so.

cash.a: Yes. Cash on completion is fully supported, alongside eSewa and Khalti. You always pay after the job is done. We never ask for payment in advance, and no professional should ever ask you to send money outside the app.

badWork.q: What if the work isn't done properly?
badWork.a: Report it from the booking within 48 hours and we'll send someone back to put it right at no extra cost. If it still isn't resolved, we refund the job. Repeat complaints affect a professional's trust score, which is why the scores on their profiles are worth reading.

checks.q: How do you check the professionals?
checks.a: Government ID and a citizenship or licence check before anyone takes a job, plus a skills assessment for the trade they're registering in. Their completion rate and rating come from real finished bookings, not self-reported claims.

safety.gas: Don't light a flame or touch any switch — open the windows, close the cylinder valve if you can reach it, and step outside.
safety.burning: Switch off at the mains if you can reach it safely, and don't use that switch or socket again until it has been checked.
safety.liveWire: Switch off at the mains and keep everyone away from the wire until an electrician has been.
safety.unseenPhoto: We couldn't look at your photo just now, so check it yourself: if you can smell gas, or see sparking, scorching or a bare wire, switch off at the mains, don't light a flame, and call us instead of booking.

fallback.generic: We'll match you with the right professional — tell them the details and they'll confirm the price before starting.
fallback.plumbing-emergency: This can cause damage fast, so we'll push you to the front of the queue and send whoever is closest.
fallback.plumbing-leak: Most leaks are a washer or a joint — usually a single visit, and the plumber will carry the parts.
fallback.plumbing-blockage: Blockages get worse if you keep using the fixture. A plumber will clear it and check what caused it.
fallback.plumbing-water: Usually the pump, the inlet valve or an airlock. The plumber will trace it back from the tank.
fallback.electrical-emergency: Treat this as urgent — switch off at the mains if you safely can. We'll dispatch the nearest electrician.
fallback.electrical-fault: An electrician will find whether it's the circuit, the fitting or the supply before quoting anything larger.
fallback.ac-cooling: Weak cooling is usually a dirty filter or low gas. Servicing is cheaper; a refill costs more.
fallback.appliance: The technician diagnoses on site and tells you the part cost before doing any work.
fallback.pest: Priced by the size of the flat and the treatment. Most jobs need one visit plus a follow-up.
fallback.cleaning: Cleaning is booked by hours and flat size, so you'll see the exact price before confirming.
fallback.carpentry: A carpenter will look at whether it's a repair or a replacement, and price the two separately.
fallback.painting: Painting is quoted per square foot after a site visit — the range is wide until someone measures.
fallback.tank: Tanks are priced by capacity. Most households do this twice a year.
fallback.movers: Quoted on distance, floor level and how much you're moving — a survey call settles it in minutes.

intro.title: Apply to work with us
intro.lead: We check who you are and what you can do, separately. It takes about fifteen minutes and you can stop and come back — everything you enter is saved as you go.
intro.needCitizenship: Your citizenship certificate or National ID
intro.needAccount: The bank account or eSewa number you want to be paid into
intro.needReferences: Two people who can vouch for your work
intro.timing: We answer within three working days. If we need anything else, we call you — we do not leave people waiting without a word.
intro.seeded: We already have your name, trade and ward from the form. Check them as you go.

status.submittedBody: We have everything. Somebody is reading it and we answer within three working days.
status.approvedBody: Your listing is live. You start on a settling-in period — a couple of jobs at a time — and that lifts on its own as work comes in.
status.rejectedBody: Here is why, and what would change it:
status.rejectedRetry: You can apply again once you have sorted this out. We keep your documents for 90 days so you will not have to photograph everything twice.

consent.title: Before we ask for your papers
consent.lead: We are about to collect documents that identify you, including a photograph of your face. You should know exactly what happens to them before you hand them over.
consent.whatWeCollect: We collect your citizenship certificate or National ID, your PAN if you have one, your police clearance, a photograph of your face, and your skill certificate if your trade has one.
consent.yourFace: A photograph of your face is biometric information. Nepali law treats it as its own category and so do we: it is used only to check that the person in the document is the person applying.
consent.why: To check that you are who you say you are, and that you can do the work. Two separate questions, and a certificate that answers one says nothing about the other.
consent.whoSees: Our own reviewers, and nobody else. No customer ever sees any of it.
consent.howLong: Until a year after you stop working with us. If we cannot accept your application, 90 days — and the moment a later application of yours is approved, the old set is deleted straight away.
consent.agree: I have read this and I agree
consent.mustAgree: Please tick the box so we know you have read it.

triageAccuracy.title: Was the triage right
triageAccuracy.lead: The one AI answer in this product, measured against what the customer went on to do. Counts only: nothing here proposes a change to the prompt, the price bands or the keyword rules.
triageAccuracy.notAFinding: These are counts, not findings. Every number carries the sample it came out of, because a rate over a dozen bookings is a number and a rate over a thousand is evidence — and they look identical without it. There is no threshold on this screen on purpose: nobody knows yet what a good agreement rate looks like here, and a line drawn now would freeze a guess into the product as a standard.
triageAccuracy.unreadable: That could not be read. It is not the same as there being nothing — do not read it as a zero.
triageAccuracy.ofTotal: {pct}% — {n} of {count, plural, one {{total} row} other {{total} rows}}

coverage.title: How much of this is measurable
coverage.lead: A booking can be compared only if it carries the triage that produced it. Somebody who came straight to the catalogue has no triage to attribute their booking to, and that is a fact rather than a gap.
coverage.attributed: Bookings we can trace to a triage

category.title: Did they book what it said
category.lead: Agreement between the trade the triage named and the trade the customer actually booked. A disagreement is not automatically a miss — somebody can read a correct answer and still book the other job they had been putting off.

band.title: Where the final figure landed
band.lead: Against the range the triage card printed, before the customer had chosen anybody. Above is a customer surprised by a bill; below is a quote that put somebody off for no reason. Unsettled jobs have no answer and are not counted.

hazard.title: What each safety detector said
hazard.lead: The text guard reads what was typed; the photo read is the model's. Until now only the winner was recorded — the text guard beats the photo whenever both fire — so agreement between them has never been countable. These are each detector's own reading.

mix.title: Which path answered
mix.lead: The product always answers, which means a silent fallback looks exactly like a working model. This is the count that tells them apart.

latency.ms: {ms}ms over {count, plural, one {{n} request} other {{n} requests}}

fallbackWhy.title: Why the keyword matcher answered
fallbackWhy.lead: Counted over the fallback answers only, not over all traffic. Until a key was set every one of these had the same cause, so the distinction that matters now is whether a key was in place: without one this is a setup step, with one the product is configured, reads as healthy everywhere, and is still not using the model.
fallbackWhy.keyRejected: The key is set and was refused
fallbackWhy.providerFailed: The key works; the model timed out, errored or throttled us
fallbackWhy.answerRejected: The model answered and we rejected the answer
fallbackWhy.notRecorded: Written before we kept the reason
